author: Template maintainers
name: .NET 10 service with OpenSpec and Claude Code guardrails
description: A .NET 10 solution with a layered profile, executable architecture rules, a single check entry point, a real OpenSpec installation and a project-scoped Claude Code context.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic dotnet restore after creation.

manualInstructions.text:
1. npm ci                              (installs the pinned OpenSpec CLI)
2. node tools/repo.mjs init --config project.config.json
   (records the repository as initialized and regenerates the derived context;
    the template engine has already applied the name substitutions)
3. node tools/repo.mjs doctor          (verify the toolchain and the OpenSpec integration)
4. node tools/repo.mjs check           (run every check)

openspec/changes/ is intentionally not copied: a new application starts with no
change history. Requirements go in openspec/specs/ as you write them.

$comment: One set of sources serves both start paths. The substitution token is declared once, in
tools/rename.manifest.json; sourceName here mirrors it, and
tools/tests/rename-manifest.test.mjs fails if the two drift apart — including the exclude
lists, so a file the GitHub-template path protects cannot be rewritten by the dotnet new path.
Only the name is a template parameter. Everything else — the architecture profile, the module
registry, the documentation language, the optional integrations, the archive gate policy — is
set in project.config.json and applied with `node tools/repo.mjs sync`. Exposing them here as
well would mean two places to change one value.
